meta_desc: NCERT Class 12 Maths Matrices Exercise 3.1 solutions: order of a matrix, number of elements, possible orders and equality, with a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Matrices Exercise 3.1 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the basics from Exercise 3.1 — order of a matrix, counting elements, possible orders and equality. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Matrices, order and elements

questions.q: A matrix has 3 rows and 4 columns. What is its order?
questions.explanation: Order is always written as (rows) × (columns). Three rows and four columns give the order 3 × 4.

questions.q: How many elements are there in a matrix of order 2 × 5?
questions.explanation: The number of elements equals rows × columns, so 2 × 5 = 10 elements.

questions.q: A matrix has 12 elements. Which of these is NOT a possible order for it?
questions.explanation: A possible order must multiply to 12. 5 × 2 = 10, not 12, so it is impossible. The rest all give 12.

questions.q: How many possible orders are there for a matrix having exactly 6 elements?
questions.explanation: 6 factorises as 1×6, 6×1, 2×3 and 3×2 — four ordered pairs, so four possible orders.

questions.q: When are two matrices A and B said to be equal?
options: They have the same order and equal corresponding elements
They have the same number of elements
They have the same order only
questions.explanation: Equality needs both: the same order AND a_ij = b_ij for every position. Same element count alone is not enough.

questions.q: A matrix A = [a_ij] of order 2 × 2 has a_ij = i + j. What is a_21?
questions.explanation: For a_21 take i = 2 and j = 1, so a_ij = i + j = 2 + 1 = 3.

questions.q: If a matrix has exactly 7 elements, how many possible orders can it have?
questions.explanation: 7 is prime, so its only factor pairs are 1×7 and 7×1 — just two possible orders.

questions.q: A square matrix of order 3 has how many elements?
questions.explanation: A square matrix of order 3 is 3 × 3, so it has 3 × 3 = 9 elements.

faq.q: What is meant by the order of a matrix?
faq.a: The order tells you the size of a matrix, written as (number of rows) × (number of columns). A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns has order 2 × 3 and contains 6 elements.

faq.q: How do I find the number of possible orders for a given number of elements?
faq.a: Count the ordered factor pairs of that number. For 8 the pairs are 1×8, 8×1, 2×4 and 4×2, giving four possible orders. If the number is prime, there are only two orders.

faq.q: What does a_ij mean in a matrix?
faq.a: a_ij is the element sitting in the i-th row and j-th column. If a rule such as a_ij = 2i + j is given, substitute the row number for i and the column number for j to build each element.
Two matrices are equal only if they have the same order and every pair of corresponding elements is equal, that is a_ij = b_ij for all i and j. Matrices of different orders can never be equal.
